newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products pick themselves up after falls.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products pick themselves up after falls.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were nervously steadier on Thursday after recent tumbles.
Gas oil firmed 25 cents on futures and premiums showed signs of recovering from a spell in the doldrums.

A Russian was done at cif high Med flat into Greece. Another was offered at cif high Med flat basis Genoa and a third was done at cif high Med -$0.25 cif Genoa. A major trader offered a cargo of 0.5 percent sulphur heating oil at fob high Med +$3.50 loading December 20-24, up from around +$1.75 a tonne for similar cargoes a week ago.

Turkish state oil company Tupras has tendered to buy three cargoes of 0.7 percent sulphur heating oil. One cargo is for delivery in December 20-25, one is for January 1-5 and one for January 5-10, traders said.
Gasoline steadied after news that a fire had knocked out a huge catcracking unit at Tosco's Bayway refinery lifted New York Harbor prices by over a cent a gallon, but trade was thin.
Premium unleaded cargoes were assessed around $1 up from Wednesday's sharply lower levels at $218 a tonne cif Med.
Naphtha was nervously steady as today's crude gains looked shaky in late business.
Traders said that because of the dearth of demand and physical cargoes were pegged notionally around $216-$220 at tonne cif Med.
Romania was the focus again in the fuel market amid news Renel may have to buy an extra 340,000 tonnes this winter in addition to the planned 1.3 million because of gas supply cuts.

High sulphur cracked cargoes were pegged around $106-107 fob Med while low sulphur material was heard offered as low as $136 cif Med. Supplies look good although sellers report no real difficulty in shifting material.
"Recent drops have reflected crude losses," said one trader.
